SEO.label: Local SEO
SEO.tagline: Show up on Google or watch competitors take your calls
features: Keywords locked to your trade + service area — not generic terms
Every service page optimized so Google knows what you do
Google Business Profile fully built out (the #1 lead driver for contractors)
Monthly content — blog post + page updates
Local citations + directory listings
Monthly ranking report — you see exactly where you stand
benefits: Free traffic that compounds — every job from SEO has zero ad cost
You own it — can't be cut off like paid ads
Page-1 ranking = market leader in their eyes before they even call you
Higher intent than paid — people searching organically are ready to buy
SEO.social_proof: Top 3 map pack results capture 70%+ of calls — everything below that is invisible. That's the position this program is built to take, and we show you the movement in every monthly report.
SEO.ideal_for: Contractors with solid reputation but limited online visibility
SEO.on_phone: When someone in {city} searches '{trade_lower} near me' right now — are you one of the first 3 names they see? You've got {gbp_review_count} reviews to work with, but reviews only matter if Google is surfacing you first. That's what this fixes.
SEO.training_note: Lead with the visibility question. Get them to say 'no I'm not showing up.' That's the close. If gbp_review_count is orange, skip that part and just go straight to the visibility question.

features: Full campaign build from scratch — Search + Local Service Ads if eligible

Scale up in busy season, throttle in slow season
Pairs with SEO to own the entire first page

Google Ads.ideal_for: Contractors who need leads NOW and can't wait 90 days
Google Ads.on_phone: If someone searched '{trade_lower} in {city}' on Google right now, would your ad show up? We can put you at the top of that page within a week.
Google Ads.training_note: Speed is the entire PPC pitch. SEO takes months. Ads work in days. Keep that contrast sharp.

Content Pack.on_phone: Are you posting on social at all right now? ... We handle the whole thing — every graphic, every caption, every month. You just hit post.

Website.tagline: A site that actually converts — not a digital business card
Website.billing: one-time — Landing $1,000 / HTML Starter $3,000 / HTML Standard $5,500 / HTML Advanced $8,500
features: Built for local search — not just looks
Mobile-first — 80%+ of contractor searches happen on a phone
Clear call-to-action on every page
Contact form with auto-response
Service pages built to rank for trade + city terms
Fast — Google penalizes slow sites
benefits: Converts visitors instead of letting them bounce
Ranks — built with SEO foundation from day one
Shows your work properly — gallery, before/afters, testimonials
Yours — no monthly fee, no platform dependency
Website.social_proof: Most contractor websites fail the 5-second test — a visitor can't tell what you do, where you work, or how to call you. We fix all three on every page.
Website.ideal_for: Contractors with no site, an outdated site, or a site that doesn't show up on Google
Website.on_phone: If I pulled up {business_name} right now and put it next to your top competitor — which one would a homeowner call first? That's the question the site needs to answer in 5 seconds.
Website.training_note: Pull up their actual site during the pitch if you can. Real feedback on their real site lands harder than anything you can describe.

audit_hook.reframe_opener: I hear you — and you might be right that the site looks fine. But looking good and converting are two different things. Most contractor sites look acceptable and lose 80% of visitors because there's no clear reason to call. Can I show you something specific on {business_name}'s site?
audit_hook.three_problems: Three things I see on most contractor sites that kill conversions: no phone number visible without scrolling, service area buried or missing, and no social proof above the fold. A homeowner who has to work to find your number calls someone else.
audit_hook.proof_line: Here's a real example — [name a client or outcome]. Same trade, similar market. Before the rebuild they were invisible on Google. After — first page for their core terms in 8 weeks.
audit_hook.close: I can put together the audit with the specific gaps on {business_name}'s site and a fixed-price proposal to fix them. Want me to send that over?
audit_hook.upsell_at_delivery: Once the site is live and converting, the next move is making sure people can find it. That's when SEO becomes the obvious add-on — same foundation, now we build traffic on top of it.

objections.too_expensive: What were you expecting? ... [let them anchor] ... What's your average job ticket? At that number, one job from the new site pays for itself. The question is how many you're leaving because the current site loses them.
objections.need_to_think: What specifically do you need to think about? I'd rather talk through it now than have it sit.
objections.already_have_someone: How long has your current site been up and when was the last time it brought in a cold lead? I'm asking because most contractor sites are set up once and left — they're not built to rank or convert over time.

Reputation.label: Reputation Management
Reputation.tagline: Reviews win the job before you ever pick up the phone
features: Automated review requests after every job
Review response drafting — every review gets a reply
Negative review triage — flag and respond before damage spreads
Monthly reputation report
Review platform monitoring — Google, Yelp, BBB
benefits: Map pack ranking is directly tied to review velocity — more reviews, higher rank
Homeowners filter on reviews before they contact anyone
Automated — you do nothing after setup
Negative reviews addressed before they become referral killers
Reputation.social_proof: Review count and recency are the #1 local ranking signal Google uses for map pack placement. Contractors who actively manage reviews rank above contractors who don't — regardless of how long they've been in business.
Reputation.ideal_for: Any contractor with fewer than 50 Google reviews or reviews older than 30 days
Reputation.on_phone: You're at {gbp_review_count} reviews right now. Your top local competitor — do you know how many they have? Because map pack placement is largely a review velocity game. The guy actively getting reviews every month is the guy in the top 3.
Reputation.training_note: If gbp_review_count is low, just say the number. Let it land. Most contractors don't realize how few they have until they hear it out loud.

Email Marketing.social_proof: Remodeling and GC clients see the biggest ROI from email because of the long decision cycle. A homeowner who gets 3 touches from you over 90 days remembers your name when they're finally ready to move.
Email Marketing.ideal_for: GCs, remodelers, or any contractor with a long sales cycle
Email Marketing.on_phone: What happens to a lead who fills out your form but isn't ready to start for 3 months? Right now, do you have any system that keeps {business_name} in front of them until they are?
Email Marketing.training_note: Most contractors lose leads not because the lead said no — but because they went cold and forgot who called them. Email solves that automatically.

One system where every piece works together, instead of juggling four or five different vendors who don't talk to each other.

total_domination.tagline: Own your market completely — every channel, every touchpoint

total_domination.on_phone: Total Domination is for contractors who want to own the market, not just compete in it. You've got SEO, GBP, reputation, content, email, paid ads running, and an AI system that responds to every lead instantly. $7,500 a month. price_too_high.trigger: That's more than I want to spend
responses: What were you expecting? [Let them anchor.] Got it. What's your average job ticket? At that number, how many extra jobs a month would it take to cover the investment? Because that's the math we need to look at.
Which part specifically feels like too much — the total, or one of the services in there? Because there's a version of this that starts smaller and scales up as results come in.

need_to_think.trigger: Let me think about it / I'll get back to you
responses: Of course. What part specifically — the price, the timing, or whether this would actually work for {business_name}? I'd rather talk through it now than have it sit for 2 weeks.
Totally fair. What would make you feel confident enough to move forward? I want to answer the actual question, not just follow up in a week and ask if you've decided.

need_spouse_partner.trigger: Need to talk to my wife / partner
responses: Makes total sense. When do you think you'll be able to sit down together? I'd actually love to get on a quick call with both of you — 15 minutes — so I can answer her questions directly instead of playing telephone.
Absolutely. What's her biggest concern usually going to be — the price, whether it works, or something else? I can put together something specific that addresses it.

tried_before_didnt_work.trigger: We tried marketing before and it didn't work
responses: What did you try? Because most of what gets sold to contractors doesn't work — it's templated, not built for your trade or your market. I only do {trade_lower}s. That's the whole difference.
What specifically didn't work? Because 'marketing didn't work' usually means one of three things — wrong channel, wrong message, or no follow-through. I want to know which one so I don't repeat it.

too_busy_to_onboard.trigger: I'm too busy to deal with this right now
responses: The onboarding is one 20-minute call. After that we handle everything. You don't need bandwidth — you just need to send me logins. That's the whole ask from your side.
I hear you — that's exactly why most contractors who are busy don't fix their marketing until they're slow. The setup happens when you're busy so the leads come in when you're not.

already_have_someone.trigger: We already work with an agency
responses: Good — what specifically do they handle? Because most agencies doing contractor work are generalists. They do dentists, restaurants, everyone. We only do contractors. Depending on what they cover, there might be a gap worth talking about.
Are you happy with the results? I ask because the bar for contractor digital marketing is low and most generalist agencies don't clear it. What metric are you watching to know it's working?

price_deflection.when_they_ask_price: Depends on what you actually need — I'd be guessing right now. Let me understand {business_name} first and I'll give you a real number, not a range I pulled out of thin air. Takes 10 minutes.
